summary: The audit checks three graduate COMPLIT courses and 20 units in all, every course letter graded where a letter grade is offered. You move in by hand the three graduate courses in your second literature's department, and mark the literary theory seminar, the two non-native languages, and that two of the COMPLIT courses originate in a department other than your own.

qJQV2IOX.why: "A knowledge of at least two non-native languages" "A minimum of six graduate courses: Three graduate courses must be in the department of the second literature ... Three graduate courses must be in the Department of Comparative Literature, including: A seminar in literary theory or criticism". Graduate courses are read as 200 and above; cross-listed courses count as COMPLIT. "At least two of the three courses in Comparative Literature should originate in a department other than the one where the student is completing their degree": the audit does not know the student's department, so this is a check by hand (ov-origin).

program.why: Grading: "PhD students in the department must take required courses for a letter grade if available". Every course in the minor is a required course. The "expected to earn a grade of B+ or better" is reviewed by the faculty, not a floor.
